comments.content: - **server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/search/SearchService.java:558** — The compatibility check uses the channel version stored on the original `ShardSearchRequest`, not the channel carrying the current continuation. In a rolling-upgrade cluster, start a scroll through an old coordinator, then continue it through a new coordinator with `error_trace=false`; the stored old version forces `header=true`, so the failure is neither logged nor stripped and its stack trace is incorrectly transported.

- **x-pack/plugin/async-search/src/internalClusterTest/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/search/AsyncSearchErrorTraceIT.java:180, 214, 248** — These submit a second async search with `wait_for_completion_timeout=0ms` and immediately assert the log expectations without polling that search to completion. On a busy node, lines 180/248 return before shard execution logs anything, causing intermittent failures; line 214 can pass its “unseen” assertion before an incorrect log is emitted, producing a false positive.

## Defect 1 — `addUnseenLoggingExpectations` registers every (node × shard) expectation under the *same* name, so the "no logging" tests assert absence for exactly one combination

**File:** `test/framework/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/search/ErrorTraceHelper.java`, hunk `@@ -45,4 +54,63 @@` → new-file lines ≈96–115; the duplicate literal is at ≈line 101:

```java
new MockLog.UnseenEventExpectation(
    "Tracking information ([nodeId][indexName][shard]) and exception logged before stack trace cleared",
```

The loop registers `numShards × numNodes` expectations and gives **every one** this identical name. The sibling method in the same diff, `addSeenLoggingExpectations` (≈line 65), carefully formats the shard number into the name so each expectation is unique — the unseen variant has no such discriminator. `MockLog` expectations are addressed by name (the `addExpectation`/`assertAllExpectationsMatched` API and the per-name failure diagnostics), so each identical-name registration replaces the previous one: only the **last (node, shard) pair** is actually asserted; the other `numShards × numNodes − 1` combinations are silently dropped.

**Concrete failure scenario:** a regression that makes a data node emit the `Clearing stack trace before transport:` debug line for, say, shard 0 on the first node while `error_trace=true` (exactly the regression `testNoLoggingInSearchFailingQueryErrorTraceTrue` — `qa/smoke-test-http/.../SearchErrorTraceIT.java` ≈lines 150–163 — and `testLoggingInAsyncSearchFailingQueryErrorTraceTrue` — `x-pack/plugin/async-search/.../AsyncSearchErrorTraceIT.java` ≈lines 185–216 — were written to catch) will go undetected if the surviving registration covers a different node/shard: the suite passes green despite the "no logging" contract being violated. The Javadoc on the method (≈lines 94–96) explicitly promises "an unseen expectation is added for each combination of node … and shard", so the effective coverage is one combination, not n×m. (Decisive check that is impossible here: `MockLog`'s storage — `Map<String, …>` keyed by name would produce the collapse described; a flat list would not, though it would leave every failure message pointing at the same ambiguous name.)

## Defect 2 — async-search logging tests assert on a background execution they never await

**File:** `x-pack/plugin/async-search/src/internalClusterTest/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/search/AsyncSearchErrorTraceIT.java`, hunk `@@ -136,6 +150,106 @@` — `testLoggingInAsyncSearchFailingQueryErrorTraceDefault` at ≈lines 153–183 (the same pattern in the `False` variant ≈lines 217–249): the first submit is polled to completion and its events all fire *before* `MockLog.capture`, so the seen expectations can only be satisfied by the **re-submitted** search at ≈line 180 (`getRestClient().performRequest(searchRequest)`). That request carries `wait_for_completion_timeout=0ms` + `keep_on_completion=true` from the original submit (≈lines 167–168), so `performRequest` returns while the search is still executing asynchronously, and `mockLog.assertAllExpectationsMatched()` at ≈line 181 runs immediately afterwards. Whether the assertion can succeed is therefore decided by an un-awaited, in-flight search: a slow or contended node (CI pause, thread-pool saturation, GC) pushes the shard failures past the assertion window. If `assertAllExpectationsMatched` does not block on the seen-latch the failure is deterministic-timing-dependent; if it does block with a finite timeout it is a flake — either way the test asserts events produced by execution it never synchronised with, unlike the equivalent synchronous `SearchErrorTraceIT` tests where `performRequest` returns only after the search (and its logs) finished. (Decisive check not available: the `SeenEventExpectation.assertMatched`/`awaitMatched` semantics in `MockLog.java`, which the diff hunk `@@ -316,6 +316,43 @@` only touches partially.)

## What I could not verify (material missing)

The workspace has no checkout, so the following load-bearing assumptions could not be confirmed against source: (a) whether `MockLog` stores expectations in a name-keyed map (Defect 1 mechanism); (b) whether `assertAllExpectationsMatched` waits on the seen-latch (Defect 2 severity); (c) that the production refactor's `request.getChannelVersion()` (from the stored `ShardSearchRequest` in the scroll/fetch/rank-feature paths) equals the old `channel.getVersion()` for scroll continuations on re-established connections — on paper it is the version of the *original* query receipt, not the continuation's channel, a divergence that only matters in a mixed-version window and which I did not report as a defect for that reason.

**DEFECT 1: `test/framework/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/search/ErrorTraceHelper.java:107-110`**  
`addUnseenLoggingExpectations` builds regex patterns with **unescaped brackets**. The pattern `format("[%s][%s][%d] ...", nodeId, index, shard)` produces e.g. `[node1][test2][0] Clearing stack trace before transport:`. When `MockLog.UnseenEventExpectation` compiles this as a regex (via `Pattern.compile`), `[node1]` is a character class matching any of `n,o,d,e,1` — not the literal string `[node1]`.  
**Failure scenario:** A test calls `addUnseenLoggingExpectations` (used when `error_trace=true` to verify no logging occurs). Logging *does* occur (bug in production code), but the malformed regex fails to match the actual log line, so `assertAllExpectationsMatched()` passes incorrectly — the test gives a false green.

---

**DEFECT 2: `server/src/test/java/org/elasticsearch/search/SearchServiceTests.java:177-178`**  
Test expectation hardcodes `\[node\]` for the node ID: `format("\\[node\\]\\[%s\\]\\[%d\\] ...", index, shardId)`. Production code logs `clusterService.localNode().getId()` (line 563 in `SearchService.java`). The test passes `createClusterService(threadPool)` as the cluster service — if that mock returns any node ID other than `"node"`, the pattern mismatch causes `assertAllExpectationsMatched()` to fail.  
**Failure scenario:** Run the test with a `ClusterServiceUtils.createClusterService` implementation that returns a different node ID (e.g., `"test-node"`). The test fails despite correct production behavior.

---

**DEFECT 3: `server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/action/search/SearchTransportService.java:459,471`**  
`ChannelActionListener` is constructed with only `channel`, dropping the second `channel.getVersion()` argument. The diff does not show `ChannelActionListener`'s constructor. If it requires two arguments (as the old call site implied), this is a compile error or runtime `NoSuchMethodError`.  
**Failure scenario:** Compile the module, or run any search transport path — classloading fails at `SearchTransportService.registerRequestHandler` if the two-arg constructor was the only one.

---

**DEFECT 4: `test/framework/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/search/ErrorTraceHelper.java:83-86`** (latent fragility)  
`addSeenLoggingExpectations` builds `nodesDisjunction = format("(%s)", nodeIds.joining("|"))` → `(node1|node2)`. This is then embedded in `format("\\[%s\\]...", nodesDisjunction)` → `\[(node1|node2)\]...`. This *currently works* because the outer `\[` `\]` are escaped literals and the inner parentheses form a regex group. However, if any node ID contains regex metacharacters (e.g., `node-1`, `node[1]`), the disjunction becomes an invalid or wrong regex.  
**Failure scenario:** Cluster node named `node[1]` — `nodesDisjunction` becomes `(node[1]|node2)`, regex `\[(node[1]|node2)\]` matches `[node1]` or `[node2]` (character class `[1]`), not the literal node ID.
